title: What does Achology mean by "applied psychology"?
content:
So what does Achology mean when it says applied psychology? Three things at once: psychology learned through practice rather than only read or watched; psychology used in real situations rather than kept academic; and psychology pointed at self-knowledge first, before it is used to help anybody else. The measure of learning here is competence, not comprehension.

Learned by doing

Every course carries exercises, reflection and skill-building, and the community exists so the doing happens with real people: peer practice, daily live events and mentorship turn watched material into rehearsed skill.

Competence built that way is gradual, earned through repetition, feedback and adjustment, which is why a completed course is treated as the start of learning rather than proof of it. The distinction runs through everything here.

Used in real life

The test of this education is Tuesday afternoon, not the course player. A difficult conversation handled better. A decision made more clearly. A person listened to properly rather than waited out.

The curriculum across the seven schools is taught for that transfer, which is what principle-led education means in practice: principles first, so that what you learn works in situations no lesson specifically covered. A procedure fails the moment reality departs from the script, and reality always does.

Self first, then others

The order is deliberate and it is the part most easily skipped.

Psychological insight applied outward before it has been applied inward becomes manipulation or projection. Somebody who can name every cognitive bias and has never examined their own is not equipped to help, they are equipped to diagnose people who did not ask.

Applied inward first, the same knowledge becomes the ground for responsible helping. That is why the teaching philosophy puts self-knowledge before influence, why character is trained alongside skill, and why the pathway has you receive coaching before you deliver any.

title: What is Achology's teaching philosophy?
content:
So what does Achology actually believe about how people learn? Achology's teaching philosophy rests on three convictions. Becoming wiser matters more than becoming intellectually smarter: knowledge of psychology is worth little without the judgement, self-awareness, and maturity to use it well. All people are capable of deep learning and growth: nobody needs fixing before they can start, and no entry gate decides who is allowed to develop. And self-knowledge comes first: you learn to understand yourself before you attempt to influence, help, or change anyone else.

Wisdom over intellect

Achology defines the goal of psychological education as living and helping well, not accumulating theory. A learner can name every cognitive bias and still react impulsively, mishandle feedback, and impose their agenda on the people they mean to help; the curriculum is therefore built to develop the person alongside the knowledge, through reflection, honest self-examination, and practice with real people in the community. That is also why the education is principle-led: principles transfer to situations no course predicted, where memorised techniques do not.

Growth-oriented, not diagnostic

Achology deliberately teaches from a growth orientation. Its courses do not teach diagnosis, categorisation, or treatment; they treat the people who study, and the people its students go on to help, as capable adults with room to grow rather than conditions to label. Clinical psychology does necessary work in its own domain, and Achology's non-clinical stance is not a criticism of it; it is a boundary, held clearly, about what this education is for. The full boundary lives in Is Achology therapy, counselling, or coaching?

Self-knowledge before influence

Every helping skill Achology teaches is pointed inward first. A coach who has not examined their own patterns projects them onto clients; a leader who cannot regulate themselves cannot steady anyone else. The curriculum's ordering, and the community's practice culture, both follow from this: understand yourself, then extend the understanding outward. It is the slowest route to helping others, and the only honest one.

Why the registered address matters to you

Nowhere in particular, and that is by design. There is no campus to visit because nothing is taught in a building. Courses, live events and the community reach members across countries and time zones, and membership is genuinely global.

The practical consequence worth knowing is the timetable rather than the geography. Live events run on UK time, so members further afield choose the sessions that suit their day, and the community itself runs continuously.

Contacting Achology

title: How long has Achology been operating?
content:
So how long has Achology actually been going? The company was founded in 2017, as The Academy of Modern Applied Psychology, in Scotland. The teaching is older than the company: Kain Ramsay was teaching applied psychology to a large global audience on Udemy before Achology existed, and the academy was built to give that teaching a proper home. In 2021 Achology Transactions Ltd was incorporated as the trading company alongside the original one.

Two dates, and why they differ

People asking this question usually want one number and there are honestly two.

The teaching goes back to 2012, when the first video-based psychology course was published. The company dates from 2017. Both are true, and conflating them is how providers quietly inflate their history, so the plainer answer is that the work is older than the business built around it.

The full timeline sets out the sequence, including the correction of an older claim that Achology was founded in 2015, which was simply wrong.

What the years since have built

Twenty eight courses across seven schools, a community running live events through the week with peer practice and mentorship, and the certification pathway through which competence is developed and recognised.

The scale is published on each course page rather than asserted here: the Diploma Course in Modern Applied Psychology (DiMAP) alone has been studied by 56,701 students, and the Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) Practitioner Training by 145,112.

Why longevity matters here at all

Not as a boast. It matters for one practical reason, which is what happens to what you buy.

An education provider's age evidences that courses are maintained rather than abandoned, that the community is a running operation rather than a launch promise, and that purchased access has somewhere stable to live. Access lasting as long as you want it is only worth something if the provider is still there, and courses being updated at no extra cost only happens where somebody is still doing the updating.

What happens to your courses if the platform changes answers the same worry from the other side.

title: Who is Kain Ramsay?
content:
So who is Kain Ramsay? Kain Ramsay is a founding member of Achology, the Academy of Modern Applied Psychology, and leads its curriculum of psychology-focused training courses. Prior to Achology, his courses were accessible on platforms like Udemy and Skillshare, where many students first encountered his teaching. Established in 2017 in Scotland, Achology reflects his practical psychology approach, now offered in a more comprehensive format through a learning community rather than just standalone videos. He co-owns and manages Achology with Karen Ramsay.

The road to Achology

Kain's route into psychology ran through lived practice rather than academia. He served in the British Army's Royal Engineers from 1996 to 2005, studied business, leadership and social sciences alongside training in coaching, counselling, Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) and Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), and worked in mentorship with ex-military veterans making the transition to civilian life.

That background shaped the conviction Achology is built on: that psychological understanding proves itself in application, and that it belongs to anyone willing to learn it rather than only to those who can pursue a degree. He is also the author of the books Responsibility Rebellion and The Ultimate Life Coaching Handbook.

How long he has been teaching this

Longer than Achology has existed. In 2012 he published what is described as the world's first video-based psychology course, and the platform followed in 2014, several years before the company itself was established. Across that time the work has reached more than 670,000 students, which is the scale that made a structured community necessary rather than optional.

One collaboration is worth naming, because it says something about how the teaching is regarded. The Skilled Helper course was built with Professor Gerard Egan, whose Skilled Helper model is one of the most widely taught frameworks in professional helping. Egan's involvement is the kind of thing that is difficult to arrange on reputation alone.

His role at Achology today

Kain leads the curriculum and remains its principal teacher. The courses across the seven schools carry his teaching, and he stays directly involved in the community where that teaching is practised, rather than appearing only in the recorded material.

His approach treats learners as capable adults, which is why Achology's education is open-entry, application-first, and honest about what it can and cannot promise. It is also why he is not the only voice here: teaching is shared with the wider instructor and editorial team, and much of what a member learns comes from practising with other members rather than from any teacher at all.

The fullest picture of his own background is on his instructor profile, and the best introduction to his work is the work itself, in the Achology Academy.

title: Is Achology an educational provider or a professional body?
content:
So is Achology the school here, or the professional body? Achology is the education provider. The Society of Modern Applied Psychology (SoMAP) is the professional body. Achology teaches: the 28 courses, the learning community, the environment where competence is developed. SoMAP evaluates: it accredits the certification pathway, assesses competency, and holds the standards for members who practise. One organisation teaches you; a separate one recognises what you can do.

Why the two are kept apart

Because an education provider that also grades its own graduates is marking its own homework.

That is the whole reason for the separation, and it is worth being blunt about it. If Achology both sold you the course and certified your competence, the certificate would be a statement by the party you paid. Nobody outside could tell the difference between a member who had genuinely demonstrated something and one who had simply completed a transaction.

Achology's responsibility ends at the quality of the education and the community it is practised in. It does not maintain practitioner registers or govern professional conduct beyond its own platform. SoMAP's independence is what gives a verified claim its meaning: the body recognising the competence is not the body that was paid for the course.

What this means for you

If you are studying for your own growth, Achology is the whole picture: courses, community, and the certification pathway as far as you choose to take it.

If you intend to practise, SoMAP is where professional recognition, standards and accountability live. It is also why the two certificates say different things: one records that you finished a course, which Achology can attest to on its own; the other records that you reached a standard, which it cannot.

Either way an Achology certification is educational recognition within this framework, never a licence or statutory qualification. What a certificate actually proves sets the boundary out plainly, and why credentials here are not inflated explains why it is drawn so carefully.

title: Is Achology a university or degree provider?
content:
So is this a university, and is what you get a degree? No. Achology is not a university, has no university affiliation, and does not award degrees or academic qualifications. It is an independent online applied psychology education provider, registered with the UK Register of Learning Providers, and its certifications are educational recognition within its own framework. That is a deliberate design rather than a limitation being worked around.

What Achology is instead

It teaches practical psychology for personal growth and helping work: 28 courses across seven schools, practised in a learning community and recognised through the Achology certification pathway, which is accredited by the Society of Modern Applied Psychology (SoMAP), an independent professional body, rather than by a university.

There are no entry requirements, no academic assessment and no dissertations. Progression is demonstrated through practice, and every claim is independently verified before it counts.

Why not seek university status

Because the two are built to answer different questions, and blurring them would damage the honest one.

A degree certifies that you studied a body of knowledge to an academic standard. Achology certifies that you practised a skill in front of people qualified to judge it. Dressing the second up in the language of the first is exactly the credential inflation Achology refuses, and the person it would harm most is the member who repeats the inflated claim to a client in good faith.

It is also why there are no entry requirements. The whole position on gatekeeping is that the only requirement for starting should be the decision to learn.

Where a university is the right answer

Universities do things Achology deliberately does not: award recognised degrees, provide research training, and open the statutory routes into regulated professions such as clinical psychology. If your goal needs a degree, this is not a substitute and does not present itself as one.

Many members already hold degrees and use Achology for the applied layer their academic study did not cover. The honest comparison is in how the approaches differ and how the certificates compare.

title: Does Achology provide crisis or mental health support?
content:
So can Achology help if you are in crisis right now? No. Achology is an education provider and does not offer crisis support, emergency services, or clinical intervention of any kind. Nothing it provides constitutes medical advice, psychological or psychiatric treatment, counselling or therapy, or diagnosis, and it operates no helpline, crisis chat, or clinical referral service. If you or someone you know is in crisis, contact a qualified professional or emergency service now: in the UK, call 999 in an emergency, get urgent mental health help through NHS 111, speak to your GP, or call the Samaritans free on 116 123, any hour of any day. Outside the UK, use your local emergency number or a crisis line in your country.

Why the boundary is firm

Crisis support requires trained professionals working within clinical frameworks: people equipped to assess risk, manage safety, and provide ongoing care. Achology's staff, facilitators, and community members are not positioned or trained for that role, and treating an education community as a substitute for crisis services puts the person in crisis at risk while placing an unfair burden on members who cannot safely carry it. The Disclaimers state this position in full, and it is held firmly because the topic matters, not despite it.

What Achology does instead

Achology teaches applied psychology for personal growth and helping work, and part of that teaching is exactly this boundary: members learn to recognise when someone needs clinical support rather than coaching, and to refer on appropriately, in line with the Achology Code of Ethics. If study here ever surfaces something you want professional help with, that is a normal and good outcome of honest self-examination; take it to your doctor or a qualified therapist, and let the education be what it is designed to be.

title: Can Achology suspend or terminate my access?
content:
So could your access ever be taken away? Yes, in specific and published circumstances. Under the Terms and Conditions, access can be suspended or terminated for a breach of the Terms, for unauthorised sharing or recording of content, for a breach of the Community Code of Conduct, or for misuse of the platform.

What follows a breach

Where access ends for one of those reasons, the Refunds Policy is explicit: no refund is due, and fees already paid may be retained to reflect the losses the breach caused.

Failed subscription payments are treated differently. Access can be suspended until valid payment details are provided and outstanding amounts cleared, with a window to put it right first, and what happens when a payment fails covers that in full.

What this means for an ordinary member

For almost everybody, nothing at all. The grounds are deliberate acts rather than accidents of everyday use.

Disagreeing with course ideas carries no consequence, and disagreement is actively expected here. Taking a long break from study carries none either: your progress is preserved and your courses wait. Letting a membership lapse is not a breach of anything.

A failed payment is a problem to fix rather than an offence. Update your payment method and the matter closes.

Why the grounds are published rather than reserved

Plenty of platforms keep a broad clause allowing them to end access at their discretion. Naming the specific grounds does the opposite: it tells you what you would have to do, which also tells you what you cannot lose your access for.

That matters in a community where members are asked to disagree openly and to bring genuine material into live sessions. People are candid in proportion to how confident they are about the rules, and vague rules quietly produce careful members.

If you believe a suspension is wrong

Suspensions are applied to specific accounts for specific reasons, so the route is direct: contact support, ask for the reason if it is unclear, and put your side plainly.

Where the cause is a payment failure, clearing it restores access. Where it is conduct or sharing, the Terms and the Code of Conduct are the reference points the decision is made against, and both are published so you can read them yourself.

title: What happens to courses if the Achology platform changes?
content:
So what happens to the courses you own if the platform changes? The commitment is that access continues through platform changes, and that is how past changes have gone: through hosting moves, interface redesigns and system migrations, purchased course access has been preserved each time. The promise is made by Achology rather than by any particular piece of software, so when the technology underneath improves, your courses move with it.

An honest note on permanence

No online business can credibly guarantee absolute permanence forever, and saying so is better than pretending otherwise.

What can honestly be pointed at is the commitment in your purchase terms, the track record of every migration so far, and a business in which withdrawing paid-for access would contradict everything else it publishes. That is a strong position and it is not magic, and the difference matters.

So treat the promise as genuine and demonstrated, and take the sensible precaution anyway: download the written resources as you go. It is ordinary practice with any digital purchase and it costs you nothing.

Why this question deserves a straight answer

Because "lifetime access" is a phrase the whole industry uses loosely, and a reader who has been burned before is right to ask what stands behind it.

What lifetime access means here is stated precisely rather than left to atmosphere: access for as long as you want it, with updates included at no extra cost. A company willing to write down the limits of its own promise is usually a better bet than one that will not discuss them.

What a change looks like from your side

Almost nothing. The place you log in improves, updated content replaces old versions automatically, and there is nothing to re-buy or re-enrol in.

If something ever failed to carry over, that is a support matter rather than a loss: contact support, and if a fault on Achology's side kept purchased content down for 7 days or more, the Refunds Policy addresses it directly rather than leaving it to goodwill.

title: Why does Achology include community access with course purchases?
content:
So why does buying a course also give you community access? Because the skills taught here are learned with people rather than only from videos. Every individual course includes three months of complimentary membership, and school bundles and the Access All Areas Pass include twelve, so the community where the material is practised arrives with the curriculum rather than as an optional extra.

The reasoning

Communication, coaching and helping skills behave like languages. Understanding the theory is the start; competence comes from using it with real people who respond in ways you did not plan for.

A learner who watches a coaching course alone has knowledge. A learner who then practises it in structured sessions, with honest feedback, develops skill. The certification pathway is built on that distinction, since progression is demonstrated through practice rather than through completions, and the gap between the two is the problem the whole design exists to solve.

Bundling the two halves prices the education as it actually works.

What this means for how you use the three months

Worth stating, because the months are often treated as a trial to evaluate and then quietly allowed to lapse.

They are not a preview of a separate product. They are the window in which the course you just bought is meant to be practised, and a member who spends them only watching has used half of what they paid for. Attending one live session in the first fortnight is the single highest-value thing a new course buyer can do.

How this differs from other models

Most platforms sell content and community separately, if community exists at all. That suits them: a marketplace's job is to deliver a course, and it does that well.

Achology's job is competence, so the community is part of the product rather than an upsell. That is also why the price sits where it does, above a marketplace course and far below a degree.

The choice stays yours afterwards

After the included months, membership continues at the standard rate unless you cancel. Continue it if the community is earning its keep, or cancel and keep studying independently: course access lasts as long as you want it either way, and the two are genuinely separate purchases.

title: Can I share my Achology account or courses with others?
content:
So can you share what you have bought with somebody else? No. An Achology purchase is licensed to one person: one purchase, one user. Your login is yours alone, and course materials may not be recorded, shared or redistributed to anyone, including family, colleagues or clients. This is set out in the Terms and Conditions, and breaching it can end your access.

Where the line sits

Using your own courses fully is the whole point of owning them. Study anywhere, take notes, apply the teaching in your work with clients, quote what you have learned in your own words.

What crosses the line is passing the materials themselves on: sharing login details, sending downloaded content to somebody else, screening course videos for a group, or teaching directly from the materials as though they were yours to distribute. Sharing and redistribution covers the detail, and what you may use in your own materials covers the professional case.

Why the rule exists, and it is not mainly about revenue

There is a commercial reason and a better one.

The commercial reason is that prices stay in the hundreds rather than the thousands because each learner buys their own access. Shared accounts erode exactly the model that keeps the education affordable and open to anyone.

The better reason is what an account actually is here. It is not a key to a video library; it is the record of one person's practice. Sessions attended, coaching delivered, claims independently verified. Two people behind one login make that record a fiction, and the thing it would destroy is the only reason an Achology certificate means anything to an outsider.

If somebody in your life would benefit

The answer is their own account. Each person's progress, certification and development record should reflect their own learning, and there is a free tier with real access if cost is the obstacle.

The consequences of ignoring this are published rather than discretionary: under the Refunds Policy no refund is due where access is withdrawn for unauthorised sharing, and access can be suspended in defined circumstances.

title: What happens if my Achology membership payment fails?
content:
So what happens if a membership payment fails? First, the thing that matters most: a failed membership payment never affects the courses you own. Course access lasts for as long as you want it regardless of any subscription. What a failed payment puts at stake is the membership itself, because Achology Membership runs on its subscription billing: you are notified by email when a payment fails, the payment system retries it, and membership access depends on the payment resolving. Updating your card in the billing settings inside the community platform puts everything back as it was.

Why payments fail, and the quick fix

The usual causes are ordinary: an expired card, a replaced card whose new details were never updated, a bank declining an international charge until you approve it, or insufficient funds on the day. All Achology payments run through Stripe on the community platform's checkout, so the fix lives in one place: open your account's billing settings there, update the payment method, and the subscription continues. If the card looks right and payments still fail, your bank is the next call, since security blocks on international transactions clear only from their side.

If membership lapses anyway

Losing membership over a failed payment is not an exit. Your account, your courses, and your progress all remain, and you can rejoin at the standard pricing whenever you choose: $7 for the first 30 days applies to new members, and returning members rejoin at $34.50 per month or $345 per year. title: What's the difference between Achology membership and courses?
content:
So what is the difference between buying a course and joining the community? A course is content you buy once and keep: the video teaching, materials and exercises on one subject, with access for as long as you want it and updates included. Membership is a subscription to the community around the courses, running while you pay for it.

What each one is

The course is a purchase. Once bought it is yours, and nothing you later do with your membership changes that.

Membership is access rather than ownership: daily live events, peer practice, mentorship groups and the discussion spaces. That difference is also why courses carry a 14-day guarantee and membership does not: you can hand back something unstarted, and you cannot hand back access you have used.

How they work together

They are halves of one education rather than two products that happen to be sold by the same company.

The course teaches the framework. The community is where it becomes skill, because coaching, helping and communication are learned with people. That is why every course purchase includes three months of membership, and why bundles and the Access All Areas Pass include twelve.

Buying membership alone gives you the community without course content, which suits somebody who wants the live environment before choosing a subject.

Choosing what you need

If you want a specific subject, buy that course. Membership comes with it, and you can decide inside the three months whether the community earns its subscription.

If you are unsure where to start, the free tier and the introductory first month let you stand inside the community before buying anything, and membership first or course first works the decision through.

If you already know you want the whole curriculum, the bundles and the Pass price the two halves together with twelve months built in.

Membership and courses together

Courses hold the curriculum; membership holds the community it is practised in. Every course purchase includes 3 months of complimentary membership, continuing at $34.50 per month afterwards unless cancelled; school bundles and the Access All Areas Pass include 12 months. title: Can I get a refund if I experience technical issues with my course?
content:
So what if something technical stops you using what you paid for? Not automatically. Under the Refunds Policy, a temporary technical issue, platform outage, or access interruption does not by itself entitle you to a refund. A refund may be considered only where both of two things are true: your access to purchased content has been down for 7 consecutive days or more, and the cause is on Achology's side rather than your device, software, internet connection, or unmet system requirements. Separately, if you are still within 14 days of buying the course, the money-back guarantee covers any reason at all, technical or otherwise.

What the 7-day rule protects

The threshold does two jobs at once. A week without access to content you have paid for is a genuine service failure, and the policy recognises it as one. A few hours of downtime during maintenance is not, because it does not dent the value of a course you will study over weeks or months, and your access to a purchased course lasts for as long as you want it, so a brief outage costs you nothing that waits for you. The policy's second condition simply locates responsibility where the cause is: platform failures and server problems are Achology's; a browser that needs updating is a fix on your side, not a refund trigger.

What to do when something breaks

First, run the quick checks that clear most access problems: reload in a different browser, clear the cache, test your connection, and try another device if one is handy. If the problem survives that, report it to support@achology.com with what went wrong, when it started, and what you have tried; that record matters, because it dates the start of any outage and gives support what it needs to fix the fault, which is the outcome that serves you faster than a refund would. If a fault on Achology's side does keep your content down for 7 days or more, raise the refund question on that same thread, where the history already proves the case.

title: Can I get a refund if I disagree with the course content?
content:
So what if you simply disagree with what a course teaches? Within 14 days of purchase, yes: the money-back guarantee on courses, bundles, and the Access All Areas Pass covers any reason at all, including disliking the teaching style or disagreeing with the approach, with no explanation required. After the 14 days, no. The Refunds Policy states it plainly: course content is interpretive, different people experience it differently, and disagreeing with an idea, or finding a topic uncomfortable, is not a fault in the product and is not grounds for a refund.

Why the policy draws the line this way

Applied psychology is a field of frameworks and perspectives rather than settled facts, and reactions to them genuinely vary: the model one learner finds valuable, another rejects. Both reactions are normal, and neither makes the content defective. Achology's Trust Statement sets out the same position: the ideas taught are open to interpretation, disagreement, and critique, and learners are treated as adults able to engage critically with material they may not accept. The 14-day window exists precisely because of this. It is the testing period in which you find out whether the approach suits you, at no risk, before the decision becomes yours to keep.

What still applies after 14 days

Your access does: a purchased course stays in your account for as long as you want it, so disagreement with one module costs you nothing across the rest. Your statutory rights under UK consumer law also stand apart from the guarantee; where the law provides a remedy for digital content that is faulty, not as described, or not fit for purpose, that remedy is unaffected, though disagreement with an idea is not a fault in that legal sense either. If your concern is something other than the ideas themselves, a broken video, missing content, or an access failure, that is a different question with different terms; raise it with support@achology.com.

content:

What you can always do is cancel: cancelling inside the community platform takes effect at once on your billing, stops all future payments, and leaves your access running to the end of the period you have already paid for. The 14-day money-back guarantee covers Achology's other products, individual courses, school bundles, and the Access All Areas Pass, but not membership.

Why membership sits outside the guarantee

Membership delivers its value the moment access opens: the member-only content, discussions, and daily live events are available from day one, and access already given cannot be handed back the way an unstarted course can. That is why the Refunds Policy treats the two product types differently, and why it says so before purchase rather than in a support reply afterwards. The pricing reflects the same logic: the monthly plan is $7 for the first 30 days and then $34.50 per month, so trying membership costs $7, not a leap of faith; the annual plan is $345 per year and renews each year unless cancelled before the renewal date.

What to do instead of a refund

If membership is not working for you, cancel it in your account's billing settings inside the community platform; no reason is needed and there is no cancellation fee. If your membership came free with a course purchase, the same applies: the complimentary 3 months continue at $34.50 per month unless cancelled, and cancelling it costs nothing while your course access continues for as long as you want it. If something has genuinely gone wrong with the service itself rather than the fit, contact support@achology.com before doing anything else: the policy allows an occasional goodwill refund at Achology's discretion, and nothing in it reduces your statutory rights under UK consumer law.

title: Can I cancel my Achology membership anytime?
content:

Cancelling ends future billing from that moment. The one cancellation people miss

Every course purchase includes 3 months of complimentary Achology Membership that continues automatically at $34.50 per month once the 3 months end. Refunding or finishing a course does not cancel it. If you bought a course and do not want the community subscription, cancel that included membership inside the platform before its complimentary period ends and it will never bill you.

Coming back later

Cancellation is not an exit from Achology. Your account and your courses remain, and you can rejoin Achology Membership at the standard pricing whenever it suits you: nothing is lost in the gap, and there is no rejoining penalty.

title: What if I change my mind after the 14-day guarantee period?
content:
So what happens if you change your mind after the fourteen days are up? Once the 14-day money-back guarantee has passed, Achology does not refund courses, bundles, or the Access All Areas Pass for a change of mind. The Refunds Policy names the situations this covers: dissatisfaction with a teaching style or approach, disagreement with an idea or framework, lack of time, engagement, or motivation, personal circumstances, and feeling you did not gain personal benefit. What you keep is the purchase itself: access to a bought course lasts for as long as you want it, so stepping away for months costs you nothing when you return.

Why the line sits there

The 14 days exist precisely so this decision can be made while a refund is still open: enough time to study the material, test the teaching style, and decide. After it, the policy treats course content the way education honestly works. Material of this kind is interpretive, and different people experience it differently; one learner finds a framework valuable while another rejects it, and neither reaction makes the content faulty. Discomfort with an idea is not a defect, and the policy says so plainly rather than leaving it to be discovered in a support reply.

What remains open to you

Three things survive the deadline. Your access: the course stays in your account, updates included, however long you pause. Your statutory rights under UK consumer law, which the policy does not reduce: where the law provides a remedy for digital content that is faulty, not as described, or not fit for purpose, that remedy stands on its own terms. And Achology's discretion: the policy allows an occasional goodwill refund outside its terms, which creates no entitlement but means a genuinely exceptional situation is still worth raising politely with support@achology.com. What is closed is only the guarantee itself.

title: How long does an Achology refund take to process?
content:
So once a refund is approved, how long until the money is back? Achology processes approved refunds promptly and asks you to allow up to 5 business days for the money to appear before following up. It returns to your original payment method, in US dollars, the currency you paid in. Straightforward requests move quickly because there is nothing to investigate.

Why five business days

Because the money crosses three organisations, not one.

Achology issues the refund, the payment processor handles it, then your bank or card provider credits it, each on its own timetable. Business days run Monday to Friday, so a refund issued on a Thursday can cross a weekend before it lands.

None of that reflects the status of your request. A refund confirmed by support is on its way while your balance still shows nothing, which is the part worth knowing so the wait does not feel like silence.

What moves fast and what does not

A 14-day guarantee claim on a course is the quick case: no reason is required, so there is nothing to assess and it simply goes through.

Requests involving a technical problem take longer, because somebody has to look at what actually happened. That is not reluctance; a claim nobody examined would be a claim nobody could stand behind.

If nothing arrives

After 5 business days, reply to your original support thread or write to support@achology.com with your order details, and the payment will be traced. How to reach support covers the routes.

One thing to check first if you paid on a card issued in another currency. Compare the credited amount against your bank's exchange rate on the day of the refund rather than the day you bought. Small differences between the two conversions are your bank's rates rather than a short refund, and they are the one cost in the process that is not Achology's.

The full terms sit in the Refunds Policy, and how to request a refund covers the step before this one.

title: Why doesn't Achology promise transformation or guaranteed outcomes?
content:
So why will nobody here promise you a result? Because no education provider controls the thing such promises claim to sell. What a course changes in someone's life depends on their practice, their circumstances, their consistency, and their honesty with themselves, none of which a platform can guarantee. Achology promises what it actually controls: the quality of its curriculum, the community in which the skills are practised, and access to purchased courses for as long as you want them. Its prices reflect those deliverables, and nothing else.

The pattern behind transformation marketing

A familiar pattern across online education prices the promise rather than the product: dramatic transformation is promised, a premium price is justified by it, and when results vary, the shortfall lands on the student's commitment. The promise does the selling, and it can never be tested at the point of purchase. Achology's position is that psychological change is real and teachable, and precisely because it is real, it cannot be sold as a guaranteed outcome. Treating readers as capable adults means telling them which part of the result is theirs to produce.

What Achology does promise

The commitments are the checkable kind. A structured curriculum across seven schools of applied psychology, taught as one integrated body of teaching. A living community through Achology Membership: daily live events, peer practice, and mentorship, where the material is rehearsed rather than only watched. Access to any course you buy for as long as you want it, updates included. And a 14-day money-back guarantee on courses, bundles, and the Access All Areas Pass, set out in the Refunds Policy, so the purchase itself carries no leap of faith.

What this means for a buyer

Read every Achology page expecting evidence rather than promises: what a course covers, how long it runs, what students report, what it costs. If a claim about your future appears anywhere, it will be conditional on your practice, because that is the truth of how applied psychology works. Buyers who want that honesty tend to be the learners the education actually serves; buyers who want a guaranteed result are better served by knowing, before spending anything, that no honest provider can sell one.

title: How does Achology's pricing reflect its anti-gatekeeping philosophy?
content:
So what does the pricing say about who Achology thinks should be let in? Achology's pricing is designed so that the only requirement for starting is the decision to learn. There are no applications, entry grades, prerequisites, or selection processes, and the prices are set where a working adult can pay them without a loan: individual courses from $97 to $299, school bundles from $987 to $1,337, and the whole curriculum through the $2,995 Access All Areas Pass. Anyone willing to learn thoughtfully and apply it responsibly can enrol today, at any age, from anywhere, and that openness is the philosophy the pricing exists to serve.

The barriers the model removes

Formal education necessarily asks a lot before teaching begins: qualifying grades, an application process, years of full-time commitment, and tuition that usually means borrowing. Those demands make sense for what a degree is, and they also mean many capable adults never get to study psychology at all. Achology's answer is structural. Fully online, so geography does not decide access. Self-paced, so the education fits around work and family rather than replacing them. Priced in the hundreds rather than the tens of thousands, so the decision is a purchase rather than a debt. And open-entry, because prior academic performance says little about someone's capacity to grow.

Why accessible is not free

Achology charges for its education because free would undermine the two things the model depends on. Quality costs money to make and maintain: the courses, the platform, and the daily live community are a real operation, not a content archive. And a price, even a modest one, marks the difference between a decision and a whim; the free membership tier and the $7 first month of Achology Membership exist precisely so you can explore seriously before that decision. Accessible means the barrier is low enough for a committed working adult, not that the education costs nothing.

What anti-gatekeeping does not mean

Open entry does not mean lowered standards. The courses hold professional depth, the certification pathway requires demonstrated competence rather than mere completion, and outcomes still depend on practice and integrity. Achology removes the barriers that decide who may start. What you make of the education after that has never been for sale.

title: Why is Achology priced higher than Udemy but lower than universities?
content:
So why does it sit between a marketplace course and a degree on price? Because the three are built to do different jobs, and the price of each reflects what it takes to run. A marketplace course is a piece of recorded content you study alone, priced accordingly. A university degree is a regulated academic qualification carried by an institution, with the cost that institutions involve. Achology, with courses from $97 to $299 and everything up to the $2,995 Access All Areas Pass, sits between them because its model does: deeper and more supported than a standalone course, without the scale, regulation, and overhead of a university.

What the difference from marketplace pricing pays for

Udemy and similar marketplaces do their job well: affordable, self-contained courses on almost any topic, often at a fraction of Achology's prices. What their model does not include is what Achology's prices carry. Achology courses are built for depth rather than volume: the Diploma Course in Modern Applied Psychology (DiMAP) alone holds 51+ hours of teaching. The seven schools are taught as one integrated curriculum rather than unrelated titles. And every course comes with the learning community where daily live events, peer practice, and mentorship run: a living operation with real ongoing costs, which is why it exists as Achology Membership rather than inside a one-off content price. If you want a single course on a single topic to study alone, a marketplace serves that well, and more cheaply.

What the difference from university pricing spares you

A UK undergraduate psychology degree costs upwards of £27,000 in tuition because it carries things Achology deliberately does not: campuses, research programmes, regulatory compliance, formal assessment, and the institutional machinery behind a recognised academic qualification. Those are real strengths when you need them; a degree remains the only route into regulated professions such as clinical psychology. Achology asks for none of that cost because it offers none of that apparatus: no entry requirements, no multi-year commitment, no academic credential, and a curriculum aimed at practical competence rather than examined theory.

Reading the price as a signal

The practical question is not which price is lowest but which job you need done. Study one topic cheaply on your own: a marketplace. A regulated qualification and a statutory career route: a university. Applied psychological skill, practised in community, starting this week from $97: that is the job Achology's pricing reflects, and the pricing page sets out every option.

title: Is Achology worth the money?
content:
So is it worth what it costs? Achology is worth the investment if you want practical psychological education you will actually engage with: structured courses from $97 to $299, a learning community where the skills are practised with real people, and a certification pathway, at a fraction of what formal study costs. It is not worth it if you want passive content to watch in the background, a quick credential, or guaranteed outcomes, because Achology's value depends on what you do with it. That is the honest shape of the answer; the rest is the detail to weigh for yourself.

What the money actually buys

A course price buys more than recorded lessons. If you need a licence to practise therapy or counselling, Achology is not that pathway and no price makes it one. title: What payment methods does Achology accept?
content:

Major credit and debit cards, including Visa, Mastercard, and American Express, are accepted, and all prices are in US dollars. The checkout page shows you exactly which payment methods are available in your region before you confirm anything, and Achology never stores your card details: they are handled entirely within Stripe's secure, PCI-compliant system.

How the checkout works

Every Buy, Enrol, and Join button on Achology.com takes you to the checkout on Achology's community platform, where Stripe handles the payment. You enter your card details there once, the payment processes, and access to what you bought opens in your account. For subscriptions, the same card is charged automatically each billing period until you cancel: monthly membership at $34.50 per month after the $7 first 30 days, or the annual plan at $345 per year, renewing annually.

All Achology prices are in US dollars. If your card is issued in another currency, your bank or card provider converts the payment at its own exchange rate and may add a conversion fee. Those charges come from your financial institution, not from Achology: the USD price you see at checkout is what Achology receives. Cards issued in most countries work wherever Stripe operates, and the checkout will show you if a payment method is unavailable in your region.

If a payment will not go through

Failed payments are usually one of three things: a card that needs updating, a bank declining an international transaction until you approve it, or a payment method Stripe does not support in your region. Check the card details and try again, contact your bank if the decline persists, and if the problem continues, contact Achology through the enquiries page so support can look at it with you.

title: Is Achology therapy, counselling, or coaching?
content:
So is this training you to be a therapist, a counsellor, or a coach? Achology teaches coaching and professional helping skills for unregulated practice. It is not therapy, not counselling, and not clinical training: it does not teach diagnosis, treatment, trauma therapy, or crisis intervention, and it offers no clinical supervision, placement hours, or route to therapeutic licensure. If your goal is to become a licensed therapist or counsellor, Achology is not the training pathway.

What Achology teaches

The curriculum covers life coaching methodologies, skilled helping models, person-centred approaches, Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) techniques, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) principles for behaviour change, communication, and facilitation, taught across the seven schools. Members learn to listen deeply, ask useful questions, create room for reflection, challenge unhelpful patterns, and support people through goal-setting, decision-making, habit change, and personal development. Some build independent coaching or mentoring practices; others use the skills inside organisations, families, and communities. Achology provides the education and the practice environment; it does not guarantee employment, clients, or income.

Where the boundary sits

Coaching and helping work focus on moving forward: clarifying goals, building capability, improving relationships, supporting decisions. Therapy focuses on healing: treating mental health conditions, processing trauma, providing clinical care. Therapy and counselling are regulated professions in most jurisdictions, requiring recognised qualifications, supervised practice, and registration with professional bodies. Achology trains members to work within the coaching and helping space, to recognise when someone needs clinical support rather than coaching, and to refer on appropriately, in line with the Achology Code of Ethics.

Your responsibility as a practising member

Members remain personally responsible for understanding what they are qualified to do, what sits outside their competence, and what legal or professional requirements apply where they practise. Achology certifications are educational recognition within Achology's framework, never a licence or statutory qualification; the full position is set out in the Disclaimers.

title: How is Achology's approach different from university psychology programmes?
content:
So how does this differ from studying psychology at a university? Achology and university psychology programmes are built for different purposes. A university degree is a regulated academic qualification: three or more years of study, formal entry requirements, tuition typically upwards of £27,000 for a UK undergraduate programme, and the only route into statutory professions such as clinical psychology. Achology is an applied psychology academy: no entry requirements, courses from $97 to $299, and a curriculum built around practical application, personal development, and community practice rather than academic assessment. Neither replaces the other; which is right depends entirely on what you want the education to do.

What universities offer that Achology does not

Honesty first. A university programme gives you a recognised academic degree, structured research training, and access to regulated career paths: if your goal is to become a clinical psychologist, a chartered psychologist, or an academic researcher, a university degree is not optional, and Achology is not the right route. Achology is not a university, does not award degrees, and its certifications are educational recognition within its own framework rather than statutory qualifications.

What Achology offers that universities typically do not

Achology's differences are real, and they matter for a different kind of learner:

  • Accessibility. No entry requirements, applications, or prerequisites; anyone willing to learn thoughtfully and apply it responsibly can start immediately, at a fraction of a degree's cost. Individual courses run $97 to $299, full school bundles $987 to $1,337, and the Access All Areas Pass, covering all 28 courses, is $2,995.
  • Breadth over specialisation. The curriculum spans seven schools of applied psychology taught as complementary perspectives rather than competing camps, where a degree usually asks you to specialise in one tradition.
  • Application from day one. Teaching centres on using psychological insight in real life and helping work, rather than working through theory and assessment first.
  • Learning in community. Members practise together through daily live events, peer feedback, and mentorship, where much university study is necessarily solitary.

Which should you choose?

Choose a university programme if you need a formal qualification, a statutory career route, or research training. Choose Achology if your goal is practical psychological competence for personal growth, coaching, mentoring, leadership, or responsible helping work, and you want to start now without academic gatekeeping or degree-level cost. Many members hold degrees already and use Achology for the applied layer their academic study never covered; others come with no academic background at all. Both are legitimate starting points here.

title: What is Achology?
content:
So what actually is Achology? Achology, The Academy of Modern Applied Psychology, is an online applied psychology training academy founded in 2017 and based in Scotland. It teaches practical psychology for personal growth and professional helping work through 28 courses organised across seven schools, a collaborative learning community, and a structured certification pathway. It is an independent education provider registered with the UK Register of Learning Providers; it is not a university, and it is not therapy.

What Achology teaches

The curriculum spans seven schools of applied psychology: The School of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP), The School of Cognitive Behavioural Psychology (CBP), The School of Life Coaching and Professional Helping, The School of Person-Centred Counselling and Psychology, The School of Mindfulness, Applied Insight and Wisdom (MIW), The School of Mental Health, Wellness and Emotional Resilience, and The School of Personal Growth and Development (PGD). Each school collects courses in one tradition, from beginner introductions to practitioner-level training, all built around applying psychological insight in real life rather than studying it academically. The full curriculum lives on the Achology courses page, and the schools are introduced on the Academy schools page.

The community and how learning works

Achology's courses sit inside a learning community rather than standing alone. Members practise together through daily live events, peer practice sessions, mentorship groups, and discussion spaces, so the skills taught in the courses are rehearsed with real people rather than only watched on video. Achology Membership is the community subscription; every course purchase includes three months of it.

Who Achology is for

Achology serves self-directed learners: people building coaching, mentoring, or helping practices; professionals adding psychological skill to work they already do; and people studying purely for their own growth. There are no entry requirements. Those pursuing recognition can progress through the Achology certification pathway, a five-level competency development programme from Achologist to Master Achologist.
